tools.name: yetty_status
tools.description: Connection + authentication status. Call this FIRST. Unauthenticated sessions can still park a website (batch tools) and start email sign-up — the response tells you exactly how.

tools.name: yetty_authoring_guide
tools.description: READ THIS BEFORE WRITING OR SENDING ANY HTML (no account needed, free, instant, no arguments). Returns yetty's exact structure rules — repeated items sharing one class, semantic class names for field labels, headings before sections, no JS-rendered content — that decide whether the site converts int

tools.name: yetty_pull_template
tools.description: Pull a ready-made Yetty template file WITH its usage contract (no account needed, free, instant). Four boilerplates, one per store surface: template:"checkout-skeleton" (cart / checkout / thank-you markup with every data-yetty-component and data-yetty-slot mark), "account-skeleton" (the buyer's /acc

tools.name: yetty_batch_start
tools.description: No account needed: start a PARKED file batch — send the site now, authenticate after. Returns park_ref (use it as batch_ref). Files are stored safely but NOT processed until the owner approves by email. EXAMPLE: yetty_batch_start {} -> {park_ref:"pk_..."} -> yetty_batch_file {batch_ref:"pk_...", pat

tools.name: yetty_batch_file
tools.description: Add ONE file to the parked batch. Args: batch_ref (the pk_... park_ref); path (relative, folders allowed); content (text) OR content_base64 (binary). Returns {received_bytes, sha256} — verify against your local copy; mismatch = resend THIS file. Send EXACT bytes, never retype.

tools.name: yetty_batch_end
tools.description: Close the parked batch. Nothing is processed yet — next call yetty_signup {email, park_ref} so the owner can approve by email.

tools.name: yetty_signup
tools.description: Link a parked upload to the owner's email: sends them an approval email. The site is processed ONLY after they click it. Args: email (the owner's), park_ref. Then poll yetty_claim_status every ~30s. Ask the owner to check their inbox.

tools.name: yetty_claim_status
tools.description: Check a parked upload. States: parked (send yetty_signup) -> awaiting-approval (owner must click the email) -> approved (returns your api_key ONCE + waiting_url — reconnect with Authorization: Bearer <api_key> for the full toolset).

tools.name: yetty_login
tools.description: Sign the OWNER in by email — no dashboard, no key copying. Works for existing accounts AND (when signups are open) new ones. FLOW: yetty_login {email:"owner@x.com"} -> {login_ref} -> the owner clicks the emailed link -> poll yetty_login_status {login_ref} every ~20s -> it returns an api_key ONCE + t

tools.name: yetty_login_status
tools.description: Check an email sign-in: pending (owner has not clicked yet) -> approved (returns api_key ONCE + reconnect instructions). EXAMPLE reconnect for Claude Code: claude mcp remove yetty; claude mcp add --transport http yetty https://mcp.yetty.ai/ --header "Authorization: Bearer <api_key>" -s user

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "yetty_claim_status" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: yetty_authoring_guide, yetty_signup, yetty_claim_status, yetty_login, yetty_login_status · Private data: yetty_pull_template, yetty_batch_start, yetty_batch_file, yetty_login · Public sink: yetty_status, yetty_pull_template, yetty_batch_start, yetty_batch_file, yetty_batch_end, yetty_signup, yetty_claim_status, yetty_login, yetty_login_status · Destructive: yetty_authoring_guide, yetty_pull_template, yetty_login_status.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: yetty_authoring_guide, yetty_signup, yetty_claim_status, yetty_login, yetty_login_status · Private data: yetty_pull_template, yetty_batch_start, yetty_batch_file, yetty_login · Public sink: yetty_status, yetty_pull_template, yetty_batch_start, yetty_batch_file, yetty_batch_end, yetty_signup, yetty_claim_status, yetty_login, yetty_login_status · Destructive: yetty_authoring_guide, yetty_pull_template, yetty_login_status

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
